title: Pre-Analysis — Outflow Valve Actuator Change Offered as a Retrofit
abstract: Closed re-analysis of the frozen outflow valve change, run on a proposal to offer it as a retrofit ahead of certification, which was rejected because the operational advisory already in place makes the case weaker rather than stronger.

sections.objective: Assess whether the outflow valve actuator change should be offered as a retrofit to the two complaining operators before the certification submission is closed, on the argument that the advisory in place is unpopular with crews.
sections.findings_summary: The proposal was rejected and returned for re-scoping. Three items were confirmed. The strongest argument against was the one nobody expected: the descent rate advisory given as an interim measure has reduced the reported event rate to almost nothing, which means the retrofit would be embodied against an evidence base that no longer exists and the operators would be paying to remove an advisory rather than to fix a fault. The second was that the trouble shooting procedure now classifies the event as a known envelope characteristic with a fifty-two per cent probability, which is the opposite of what a retrofit case needs to say. The third was that a comparable change in another chapter is making the same certification argument about transients that recover by themselves, and the two should be submitted together rather than separately.
sections.next_steps: Reject the pre-certification retrofit. Keep the advisory and continue to collect event data so that the eventual case rests on something. Coordinate the certification submission with the bleed threshold change, which is making the same argument. Revisit once the submission is closed.

similarity_seeds: a transient that recovers by itself and does not need to be annunciated

tasks.title: Measure the event rate since the advisory was adopted
Search for the same certification argument elsewhere

expected_findings.rationale: The procedure now classifies the event as a known envelope characteristic with a fifty-two per cent probability and tells the technician not to replace a component. That is the opposite of what a pre-certification retrofit case needs to say and would have had to be withdrawn to support it.
expected_findings.resolution: Procedure retained as written; retrofit case rejected.

evidence.similarity_note: Two changes in different chapters with no identifier in common, both arguing that a transient which recovers by itself does not need to reach the crew. The vocabulary is entirely different in each.

expected_findings.rationale: A bleed threshold change in pre-analysis is making the same certification argument. Submitting the two separately invites two different answers to one question.
The installation task already carries a different acceptance band for the post-modification actuator, written before the change was frozen, and it has never been validated against hardware.
expected_findings.resolution: Band to be validated at the first embodiment whenever that happens.

type_data.conclusion: Pre-certification retrofit rejected. The advisory has removed the evidence base the retrofit case would have rested on.
